notes:
Summary: evaluation for replacing in-house rule engine used for agent assist + automated refunds. Primary driver = reliability and predictable cost during 3x holiday spikes. Currently using a brittle mixture of webhooks -> lambda -> Zendesk; needs robust tool-calling layer with transactional semantics.

Recent activity:
- 2026-02-15: onsite deep-dive w/Eng + Ops (Jordan + Maya + Aurora infra). Reviewed failover pattern for ticket-create API; agreed to run end-to-end POC that injects spike traffic.
- 2026-01-27: discovery call (record ff_2026-01-27_AURORA_DISCUSSION_87X2). Covered use-case mapping, top 10 failure modes.
- 2026-01-20: sent security questionnaire; Aurora flagged retention/residency and KMS. Drive links shared.
- 2025-12-05: initial intro; high-level pricing ask.

Use-case details / requirements:
- Workloads: live chat -> agent assist suggestions (low-latency), async ticket summarization for long email threads, tool-calling to payment gateway (refunds), Zendesk ticket create/update, Salesforce case link for VIPs, automated escalations to L2 via webhook.
- Latency/throughput targets: 95th pct token latency for suggestions < 150ms; tool-call end-to-end (LLM suggestion + ticket create) < 500ms ideal, acceptable up to 2s for non-VIP flows. Peak concurrency: 6k live chats during sale spikes, average 900 qps across APIs.
- Reliability: must handle 3x baseline spikes without >1% error rate; automatic fallback to human queue if tool-call fails. Idempotency and dedup keys required for refund tool-calls.
- Observability: per-request audit id, token-level cost breakdown, per-route SLA metrics; long-term audit logs for disputes (2y).
- Security: SSO (SAML) for console, SOC2 required, customer-managed KMS for keys, EU residency option for EU customers.

Technical preferences / model routing:
- Prefer open models for embeddings/summarization but willing to run Redwood-verified variants for latency-critical agent assist. Want routing rules: VIPs -> lower-latency (higher-cost) model; overflow -> cheaper quantized model. Automatic fallback to hosted model when dedicated pool is saturated.

POC plan (agreed):
- Step 1: 1-week canary POC on Redwood hosted API using curated prompt set + synthetic spike generator (week 1). Measure latency, token cost, and tool-call success rate.
- Step 2: run dedicated pool demo (week 2) with auto-scaling policy tuned to match Aurora traffic patterns.
- Step 3: integration test with payment gateway sandbox to validate idempotency and refund flow observability.

Quotes / callouts from Aurora: "During Black Friday last year our refunds pipeline fell apart — we need a system that can retry safely without double-refunds." — Head of Ops.

Open questions / blockers:
- Can Redwood guarantee per-route rate limits and provide a documented retry/backoff strategy for tool-calling?
- Need sample audit trails for a refund event (tokenization of PII, redaction options).
- Legal wants a data residency appendix before any EU-located POC starts.

Next steps (short term):
- Deliver POC SOW and test harness by 2026-02-20 (Jordan).
- SE (Maya) to provide recommended batch sizes, KV cache settings for token cost reduction.
- Schedule payment-gateway sandbox integration session (Aurora infra + Redwood infra).
